04 Anxiety and benzodiazepines · class card

Other anxiety agents

buspirone · hydroxyzine

Practice
  1. 45-year-old man with generalized anxiety disorder, partly better after 10 weeks of sertraline alcohol use disorder, sober 1 year; drives a delivery truck wants an add-on that will not sedate him or become habit-forming examination normal → Add buspirone → buspirone, a partial agonist at serotonin 1A receptors, may be added when the response to an SSRI falls short and brings no sedation, tolerance or addiction; benzodiazepines carry risks of addiction and dependence, which he asked to avoid, and hydroxyzine is a sedating short-term add-on
  2. 34-year-old woman with generalized anxiety disorder, partly better on escitalopram an add-on drug is started; she has no daytime drowsiness months later she stops it abruptly, with no withdrawal symptoms examination normal → Serotonin 1A receptor partial agonism → buspirone partially stimulates serotonin 1A receptors and brings no sedation, tolerance or dependence; a benzodiazepine sedates and brings withdrawal, and hydroxyzine, a histamine 1 blocker, causes drowsiness
  3. 79-year-old woman with generalized anxiety disorder; sertraline started 2 weeks ago hydroxyzine added 3 days ago for agitation and poor sleep now drowsy, inattentive and confused, with a dry mouth afebrile · no clonus · reflexes normal → Anticholinergic effect of hydroxyzine → a first-generation antihistamine with anticholinergic action can bring on delirium in an older adult; no fever or clonus argues against serotonin syndrome, and onset within days of a new drug argues against dementia
